title: Stand the brick on end: less friction?
hook: Less of the brick touches the table. Does it get easier to drag?

knows: rough surfaces grip more than smooth ones
a brick has wide and narrow faces
force in newtons, read off a spring scale
doesNotKnow: that sliding friction depends on the normal force and the surface pair, not the contact area

misconception: More contact area means more friction, so a brick on its narrow face slides more easily.
objective: The learner can explain that for hard dry surfaces the steady pull equals mu x m x g whichever face is down, because friction depends on how hard the surfaces are pressed together, not on how much surface touches.

claims.text: For hard, dry surfaces, sliding friction is f = mu x N, where N is how hard the surfaces press together; it does not depend on the contact area.
claims.source: Amontons' laws of friction (1699); Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 6.1. Explanation: real contact area grows with load, not apparent area (Bowden and Tabor, The Friction and Lubrication of Solids, 1950).

claims.text: A 2 kg brick on a table with mu = 0.40 needs a steady pull of 7.8 N on any face; 1, 3 and 4 kg need 3.9, 11.8 and 15.7 N.
claims.source: 0.40 x 2 x 9.81 = 7.85 N (shown to one decimal as 7.8 N); 0.40 x 9.81 x 1, 3, 4 = 3.92, 11.77, 15.70 N. Checked in node.

claims.text: The brick is 24 x 12 x 4 cm, so its faces touch 288, 96 and 48 cm² of table; the long side has one third of the wide face's area.
claims.source: Illustrative dimensions chosen so the narrow face is one third of the wide one (brief #24); 24 x 12 = 288, 24 x 4 = 96, 12 x 4 = 48.

claims.text: A pull at steady speed equals the friction force, because the net force on the brick is zero.
claims.source: Newton's first law: constant velocity means zero net force, so the scale force balances kinetic friction.

claims.text: The rule holds for hard, dry surfaces; soft or sticky materials such as racing tyres do grip more with more area.
claims.source: Stated limitation (reveal). Rubber friction includes adhesion and hysteresis that depend on contact area and pressure (Persson, Sliding Friction, Springer 2000, ch. 13).

recall.question: A wooden crate slides across a concrete floor. You turn it onto a face with twice the area. The force to keep it sliding at steady speed…
recall.why: Sliding friction is mu x weight for hard dry surfaces; more area spreads the same weight thinner, so the force stays about the same.
